transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Thompson (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Mark Jensen (Nova - Head of ML), Sofia Alvarez (Nova - ML Eng), Liam O'Connor (Nova - SRE)

Summary (auto): quick demo of Redwood Eval/Quality Monitoring features \u00151 prompt sets, regression alerts, A/B comparisons; walked through Redwood Console, Optimize suggestions, and how to run a POC.

[00:00] Alex Thompson: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, i'm alex from redwood, this is priya our solutions engineer, we'll do a quick ~30 minute walkthrough and leave time for q&a, sound good?
[00:08] Mark Jensen: yep thanks alex, excited \u00151 trying to understand how we can catch regressions when models change and run apples-to-apples a/b tests across prompt variants.
[00:18] Priya Rao: great, so i'll share my screen \u00151 we'll start in the console, show the eval workspace where you manage prompt sets, then show the alerting for regressions and the a/b compare flow.
[00:35] Sofia Alvarez: quick note \u00151 we have an internal baseline model and a new fine-tuned variant, and we want to be sure responses don't degrade on key intents, plus we want throughput numbers for cost estimates.
[00:48] Alex Thompson: totally \u00151 typical ask. also curious about your constraints: latency targets, data residency, and whether this will run hosted or private?
[00:55] Mark Jensen: for POC, hosted is fine but long-term we'd want private (VPC) for HIPAA-ish data. latency target ~350ms p50 for 1k qps baseline, cost is also a big factor.
[01:08] Priya Rao: ok noted. in the console you can create prompt sets \u00151 we usually recommend categorizing by intent and difficulty and including gold responses. i'll open the "Eval -> Prompt Sets" tab.
[01:22] [screen share noises] 
[01:30] Priya Rao: here's a sample prompt set we shipped for a healthcare triage flow \u00151 each row is: prompt, expected/ground truth, evaluation metric (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE, semantic similarity), and tags. you can bulk upload CSVs or hook directly to your dataset storage.
[01:49] Liam O'Connor: is the CSV upload encrypted at rest? how do we manage keys?
[01:55] Priya Rao: yes, data at rest is encrypted and you can bring your own KMS for private \u00151 we'll include the KMS integration notes in the security pack.
[02:03] Mark Jensen: good. show us how regression alerts work \u00151 we want automatic notification when a metric drops 5% relative to baseline.
[02:12] Priya Rao: sure \u00151 alerting is threshold-based or delta-based. you define a baseline run (we snapshot a run id), choose metrics, and then create an alert rule \u00151 e.g., semantic_similarity < baseline - 0.05 triggers an alert and sends to slack/email or creates a ticket in Jira.
[02:30] Priya Rao: demo time \u00151 creating an alert: select baseline run -> choose metric (embedding cosine sim) -> set delta 0.05 -> action webhook to slack.
[02:41] [keyboard clacks] 
[02:47] Sofia Alvarez: are alerts per-prompt or aggregated? we need per-intent breakdowns to triage.
[02:53] Priya Rao: both \u00151 you can get per-prompt failure lists and aggregate cohort metrics; the UI also supports filter by tag/intent.
[03:05] Mark Jensen: cool. can we run A/B comparisons to compare prompt variants and model variants side-by-side?
[03:12] Priya Rao: yes \u00151 the A/B compare flow lets you upload two prompt sets or two model-run ids and will compute paired metrics with confidence intervals. we'll show an example.
[03:24] [screen flicker] 
[03:30] Priya Rao: here we ran baseline vs tuned model, metric is semantic sim and accuracy on classification intents. you can see cohort split, p-value, and an automated note that flags regressions with examples.
[03:46] Mark Jensen: nice, the example outputs look familiar. how reproducible are these runs? we want exact seedable behavior across runs for audits.
[03:55] Priya Rao: we store run metadata: model version, tokenizer hash, seed, prompt set version, and config (temperature, top_p). for private deployments we can also snapshot the model binary hash. that metadata is exportable for audits.
[04:12] Liam O'Connor: for private, networking \u00151 do you need outbound connectivity? how do we handle air-gapped options?
[04:18] Alex Thompson: we offer private on-prem with no egress and a customer-managed control plane; we'll surface the deployment options in the security doc.
[04:28] Priya Rao: quick aside on Optimize: it suggests batching/quantization and tells you the expected latency/cost tradeoffs for each quantization profile \u00151 we can run a cost simulation for your workload.
[04:42] Sofia Alvarez: can you show a run of A/B where we compare responses with the same prompt but different few-shot examples? we want to see how few-shot context shifts accuracy.
[04:52] Priya Rao: absolutely \u00151 i'll pick a prompt, create two variants with different few-shot context, kick off the compare. it runs across the prompt set and shows where variants differ, and highlights worst regressions.
[05:08] [pause - background voice] 
[05:14] Priya Rao: note \u00151 transcriptions sometimes miss tokens but core UI is deterministic.
[05:20] Mark Jensen: re: metrics \u00151 semantic similarity works but have you seen teams combine LLM-based judgement with rule-based checks? we might want a hybrid.
[05:30] Priya Rao: yes, you can add custom evaluators. we have built-in similarity, BLEU/ROUGE, hallucination heuristics, and you can plug a lambda that executes custom scoring and returns a numeric score per example.
[05:45] Mark Jensen: how are false positives handled for alerts? e.g., small shifts that are noise.
[05:50] Priya Rao: alerts have noise filters: rolling windows, minimum sample sizes, and can require sustained delta across N runs. Also you can tune the confidence threshold for A/B tests.
[06:06] Alex Thompson: switching to POC scope \u00151 for a pilot, typical deliverables: ingest your prompt set (1k-5k examples), run baseline + tuned variant, create regression alert rules, and a dashboard with cohort breakdowns. Pricing depends on token volume and whether you run hosted or dedicated.
[06:22] Sofia Alvarez: for token estimates, we run average prompt length ~180 tokens, response ~120 tokens. can you give cost projection?
[06:29] Alex Thompson: yes \u00151 with Redwood Optimize we calculate expected per-token cost after batching and caching; i'll follow up with a spreadsheet projecting cost for 1k QPS equivalent run.
[06:40] Mark Jensen: security before we go deeper \u00151 SSO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS for keys. we need SOC 2 and penetration testing reports.
[06:51] Alex Thompson: we will send the SOC 2 docs today and the penetration test summary; for SSO we support SAML/SCIM and fine-grained RBAC.
[06:59] Priya Rao: another note \u00151 for eval lineage we store run ids and you can diff two run ids which is helpful during compliance reviews.
[07:10] Mark Jensen: good. one more technical \u00151 when you compute semantic similarity, what embedding model do you use? is it pluggable?
[07:18] Priya Rao: we support multiple embedding backends; the default is a high-quality open model we manage, but you can bring your own embeddings if you want consistent vectors with your other pipelines.
[07:28] [brief pause] 
[07:35] Priya Rao: demo: i triggered a synthetic regression by swapping the tuned model \u00151 you can see alerts fired and examples pinned for triage. watch the "failed examples" widget \u00151 it shows prompt, baseline, variant, and an auto-extracted diff.
[07:51] Sofia Alvarez: that's super helpful. can we annotate failed examples and add comments for triage?
[07:55] Priya Rao: yes, there's an annotation workflow and you can assign to owners; annotations are exported to Jira or can create tasks automatically.
[08:05] Mark Jensen: for A/B, do you do bootstrapped confidence intervals?
[08:09] Priya Rao: yes, and we also compute p-values using paired tests when appropriate. the UI surfaces significance and suggests whether an observed delta is likely real.
[08:19] Liam O'Connor: on infra \u00151 for dedicated runs, how do you handle autoscaling and warm KV cache to avoid cold-start penalty during tests?
[08:28] Priya Rao: dedicated pools support pre-warming and scheduled warm windows; KV cache can be pre-populated for common prefixes. Optimize can recommend batch sizes to hit latency SLOs.
[08:41] Mark Jensen: ok promising. what's the typical time to onboard a 1k prompt set POC?
[08:46] Alex Thompson: usually 2 weeks end-to-end if we have prompt set and access to a test endpoint; includes baseline run, configure alerts, and demo of results.
[08:56] [chatter] 
[09:02] Priya Rao: stepping through the report export \u00151 csv of per-prompt scores, pdf summary with flagged regressions, and a JSON run export for audit.
[09:12] Sofia Alvarez: can these exports be pushed to our s3?
[09:16] Priya Rao: yes, export targets include s3, gs, and internal buckets for private.
[09:22] Mark Jensen: good. about model binaries \u00151 we need hashable artifacts for certifying a model. you mentioned binary hash earlier?
[09:29] Priya Rao: correct \u00151 for private deployments we can store the model artifact hash and include it in the run metadata; that helps with reproducibility.
[09:38] Alex Thompson: ok quick recap and next steps \u00151 we will: send security pack (SOC2+pen test), share sample eval prompt set and spreadsheet, propose pilot pricing, and schedule the POC run week of Jan 4. any objections?
[09:54] Mark Jensen: none. one ask \u00151 include an example of the alert webhook payload so our SRE can integrate.
[09:59] Alex Thompson: will include that.
[10:03] Sofia Alvarez: also include guidance for reducing false positives, like recommended sample sizes and noise filters.
[10:08] Priya Rao: will do.
[10:12] Mark Jensen: thanks, good demo. we'll review docs and reconvene after internal alignment.
